title: Author Identity Conflict Policy Review

task_a_safety_boundary.current_comparison: exact Python string equality, case/whitespace/punctuation-sensitive, no transformation applied

task_a_safety_boundary.claude_md_policy_exact_quote: Deterministic identifiers only for matching: Scholar_ID, DOI, ORCID, OpenAlex Author ID. Never name-based fuzzy matching for cross-attribution.
task_a_safety_boundary.602_incident_exact_nature: primary paper-ownership attribution (which researcher's profile does this whole paper belong to) was decided by name matching; fixed by making that specific decision flow only from Scholar_ID
task_a_safety_boundary.disambiguation_pipeline_scope: secondary co-author linkage only; never touches the trigger researcher's own primary link; gated by confidence threshold + human review fallback
task_a_safety_boundary.policy_tension_description: disambiguation/pipeline.py's Tier 4/5 already perform name-based (and even pg_trgm fuzzy) matching for identity linkage in production today; whether this falls inside or outside CLAUDE.md's literal policy text is a genuine, unresolved data-governance question this phase surfaces but does not resolve
task_a_safety_boundary.current_authornameraw_conflict_question_: narrower than either the 602-incident or the disambiguation pipeline's use case: UserID identity is already fixed on both sides in every examined case; the only question is whether a display-text field for that already-agreed identity is equivalent

final_decision_reasoning: normalize_name() may inform a future human-review surface but must not automatically decide populated-vs-populated AuthorNameRaw conflicts; direct proof of collision risk found this phase; the one real repository precedent (disambiguation pipeline) itself relies on human review at this confidence range, not blanket automation; option E (empty-vs-populated) is a real, narrow, evidence-backed exception but does not resolve the LOSER_ONLY_BACKFILL bottleneck since none of the 3 candidates have that shape

q1_is_disambiguation_precedent_transfera.verify_attributions_py_reconfirmed_mecha: deletes Authors rows via normalize_title(paper.Title) not in fetch_scholar_titles(scholar_id); operates on paper-title membership, not AuthorNameRaw text at all
q1_is_disambiguation_precedent_transfera.disambiguation_pipeline_structural_shape: 1-to-many identity search (one scraped name against a pool of candidate researchers) -- a wrong match reassigns a paper to the wrong person
q1_is_disambiguation_precedent_transfera.merge_time_authornameraw_structural_shap: 1-to-1 equivalence check on two strings already tied to the identical UserID on both sides -- no candidate pool, no misattribution possible
q1_is_disambiguation_precedent_transfera.conclusion: precedent proves normalize_name() is accepted in principle elsewhere in this codebase (undermining an absolute-ban reading of CLAUDE.md), but does not by itself justify reuse for the narrower 1-to-1 question -- that still requires independent risk analysis

q2_is_normalize_name_deterministic_in_al.method: called normalize_name() 20 times each on all 5 distinct real AuthorNameRaw strings from the 3 LOSER_ONLY_BACKFILL candidates (100 calls total)
q2_is_normalize_name_deterministic_in_al.result: zero variance across every call for every input

q3_can_case_only_be_safe_without_endange.tested_transformation: s.lower() only -- no punctuation stripping, no whitespace collapsing, no diacritic removal (explicitly narrower than normalize_name())
